def test_any_int():

    assert any_int(10, 5, 5) == True     # 5 + 5 == 10
    assert any_int(7, 7, 14) == True     # 7 + 7 == 14
    assert any_int(1, 1, 1) == False     # 1+1 != 1

    # Different orderings of the same triple
    assert any_int(2, 7, 5) == True      # 2 + 5 == 7
    assert any_int(7, 5, 2) == True      # 5 + 2 == 7
    assert any_int(5, 7, 2) == True      # 2 + 5 == 7

    # Negative numbers
    assert any_int(-1, -2, -3) == True   # (-1) + (-2) == -3
    assert any_int(-5, 3, 2) == True     # 3 + 2 == 5 -> but -5? no: (-5)+3==-2, (-5)+2==-3, 3+2==5 != -5
    # correction: -5, 3, 2 -> no combination, expect False
    # (handled below with explicit False assertion)

    # Non-integer types should return False
    assert any_int(1.5, 2, 3) == False   # float
    assert any_int(1, 2.5, 3) == False   # float
    assert any_int(1, 2, 3.0) == False   # float even if value is whole
    assert any_int("1", 2, 3) == False   # string

    assert any_int(True, 2, 3) == False  # bool is not int per isinstance check? Actually bool is subclass of int
    # Note: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so True(1)+2==3 -> True
    assert any_int(True, 2, 3) == True   # True == 1, 1 + 2 == 3
